rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the foundational impact of multimodal integration (rna + image) with minimal changes (singleprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, no aggregation, concat fusion). It isolates the effect of combining modalities, which is a critical design choice, and provides a baseline for comparing complexity vs performance.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from 'concat' to 'weighted' improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best next step because it directly addresses a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal changes, balancing exploration and exploitation while reducing uncertainty about multimodal integration effectiveness.

Existing evidence shows multimodal singleprofile models (config_016/017) achieve ~52.6% accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile in multimodal setup with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, isolating the impact of profile setting. It directly addresses whether multiprofile improves performance, a key design choice with sparse evidence, while maintaining consistency in encoder/fusion methods to isolate the effect of profile setting.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile setups (config_018) outperform singleprofile ones, and avgpool aggregation is effective. This experiment tests whether switching from concat to weighted fusion in the high-performing multiprofile setup (config_018) further improves accuracy, isolating the impact of fusion strategy. It exploits strong evidence for multiprofile while exploring a critical design choice with minimal changes.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation in the same setup improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It is the best next step as it explores a critical design choice with minimal changes while building on the promising multiprofile multimodal foundation.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile multimodal models with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced architecture) further improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder choice. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether better image encoders can enhance results without changing other design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) yield high performance. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 in the same setup improves accuracy, isolating the impact of the RNA representation. It balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile/weighted fusion pattern with exploration of encoder choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation (e.g., config_031) achieve high validation accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether the RNA-only variant with the same encoder and aggregation (config_005) can match this performance, isolating the impact of multimodal fusion. It directly compares modality importance while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation consistent, addressing uncertainty about whether image data adds value.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and weighted fusion (like config_031) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l (while keeping aggregation and fusion methods the same) improves performance, isolating the impact of the image encoder choice. This addresses uncertainty about whether advanced image encoders (like imagenet_vit_l) could further enhance performance in this high-performing setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, scvi_n200 RNA encoder, and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_037) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_037) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It builds on the strong foundation of config_037 while exploring a key design choice with potential for significant impact.
